clue.text: Grey skirt in the drawer

parts.note: reads like a dark grey ...-style skirt folded away in a chest of drawers, but the drawer is an artist, and the thing in their hand is a stick of burnt wood for sketching

explanation.surface: A grey skirt lies folded away in a chest of drawers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' looks like furniture; it means someone who draws. A charcoal pencil skirt is also a dark grey garment, hence 'Grey skirt'.
explanation.definitionFit: Artists sketch with this tool, and a pencil skirt in charcoal grey is also a garment.

clue.text: Dogs and poultry catch up, but not in the main text

annotationWithheld.clue: Dogs and poultry catch up, but not in the main text

clue.text: Highlights our problem in Arab love for Israel's destruction

indicators.note: the jumbled word our is placed in the middle of Arab, after its first letter
a problem with the word our means its letters are put out of order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, written as the letter O

indicators.note: destruction wrecks the country's name so that its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the country name taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A political complaint about Arab hostility towards Israel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem' rearranges OUR and 'in' sets it inside ARAB; 'destruction' turns ISRAEL into REALIS. The surface reads as Middle East politics, but 'Highlights' are lights in the sky. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The northern lights are a natural display of light in the polar sky, a spectacular highlight.

clue.text: Cold, cutting inactivity

parts.note: a chill is a coldness
axing means cutting, as with an axe or a budget

explanation.surface: A cold and cutting remark about someone's laziness.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang blend of chilling and relaxing, meaning idle lounging about.

clue.text: Seraglio almost built here?

indicators.note: letters built into a new structure are rearranged
almost the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A guess at the city where a sultan's harem palace might have been built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts SERAGLIO to SERAGLI, which 'built' rearranges. A seraglio is the women's quarters of an Ottoman palace, plausibly found in a North African capital, so the whole clue is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Algeria, once an Ottoman city where such a harem palace could stand.

clue.text: See 1 across
The Alps expedition ends badly for them

definitions.text: The Alps expedition ends badly for them

indicators.note: letters treated badly are knocked out of order
the ends of the word expedition are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Hannibal's famous crossing of the Alps ended in disaster for his animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' gives E and N from expedition; 'badly' rearranges them with THE and ALPS. Hannibal took war elephants across the Alps and most died, so the whole clue defines them.
explanation.definitionFit: Hannibal's war beasts famously perished crossing the mountains on his march to Rome.

clue.text: Briefly hint flat is a suitable location for nightlife

indicators.note: a word cut short briefly loses its last letter

parts.note: a clue is a hint
bland means flat, dull or tasteless

explanation.surface: Someone advises that a flat would be ideal for going out at night.
explanation.definitionFit: The district of a city full of nightclubs is where people go out after dark.

clue.text: They may be poets who keep an eye on the ball

definitions.meaning: writers of verse are men of lines

definitions.text: who keep an eye on the ball
definitions.meaning: football officials on the touchline watch whether the ball goes out

explanation.definitionFit: Poets write verses, so are humorously men of lines; touch judges at football watch the ball along the field's edge.

clue.text: Moving to the next line in marriage starts with a 90% reduction to income

indicators.note: the opening letter is a Roman numeral, a thousand, cut by ninety per cent to a hundred, its numeral

parts.note: a return is income from an investment

explanation.surface: A tax note on how marriage starts off by slashing your earnings.
explanation.walkthrough: M is 1000 in Roman numerals and C is 100, so a 90% cut turns the M of MARRIAGE into C. 'in' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The typewriter command that sends the printing position back to the start of a fresh row.

See 20
Henry Holmes into being stripped of registration

explanation.surface: A man called Henry Holmes is having his registration taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: Stripping each word gives ENR, OLME and NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Signing up on a list or course is the act of registering.

clue.text: Herr Sanger's changed hands for the gang

indicators.note: changed, read with hands, swaps right for left: the letters for right become those for left

parts.note: the German title taken as written

indicators.note: hands here are right and left, so each R abbreviation is exchanged for an L

parts.note: the surname taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A German gentleman named Sanger had something change ownership.
explanation.walkthrough: R and L are standard abbreviations for right and left, so changing hands turns all three Rs into Ls.
explanation.definitionFit: The notorious motorcycle club is a biker gang.

clue.text: A couple is firm that a chaperone is not required

definitions.text: that a chaperone is not required

parts.note: a couple is two, so 'two is' contracts to two's
a company is a firm

explanation.surface: A couple point out that their business needs no supervisor.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying runs 'two's company, three's a crowd': a pair needs no third person tagging along.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says a pair is happiest alone, so no escort is wanted.

clue.text: Wine drinking lover turns into a beast

indicators.note: something drinking takes another thing inside it
the word lover turns, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A man in love drinks wine and becomes an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' rearranges LOVER to OLVER, and 'drinking' takes it inside. The surface suggests drink turning a lover into a brute. 'into' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A fierce carnivorous member of the weasel family from northern forests.

clue.text: May be a hair shirt for the last to leave town

indicators.note: the last letter of the alphabet leaves, removed from the town's name

parts.note: Penzance is a town in Cornwall, England

explanation.surface: A hair shirt punishes whoever is last out of town.
explanation.walkthrough: Penzance is a seaside town in Cornwall, England. 'to leave' removes Z, the alphabet's last letter. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing a scratchy shirt was a traditional act of self-punishment for sin.

clue.text: Dodge has broken down despite circling soft-top

indicators.note: the jumbled letters circle round the other piece, which goes inside
a word broken down falls apart and its letters are reshuffled
the top of soft is its first letter

explanation.surface: A car has broken down even though its convertible roof is off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken down' makes SIDETEP from DESPITE and 'circling' wraps it round S, the 'top' of soft. Dodge is also a car make, which sets the scene. 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidestep is to avoid something by stepping aside.

parts.note: a cache is a hidden store or hiding place

clue.text: See 13

clue.text: 13 feature from crazy backwards people

indicators.note: the word for crazy is read backwards

parts.note: mad means crazy
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: Something taken backwards from crazy people.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 refers to the HELLS of 13 across: eternal punishment is the defining feature of hell. 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal condemnation is what the infernal regions are known for.

clue.text: See 3
Cake with calories out? Not so!

indicators.note: letters knocked out of order are rearranged

explanation.surface: A slimmer asks if a cake has had its calories taken out, and is told no.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of CALORIES are the answer's letters plus S and O: 'Not so' says take those away, and 'out' scrambles the rest. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A long choux pastry filled with cream and topped with chocolate.

clue.text: It's good in youth then to have frivolous talk

definitions.text: It's good in youth then to have frivolous talk

parts.words: It's good in youth then to have frivolous talk
parts.note: the first half invites its opposite: what is good in youth is then ..., and those three words run together give a word for light banter

explanation.surface: An elder's view that idle chatter suits the young.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap good for bad and youth for age: 'bad in age' run together spells the word for frivolous talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Playful, teasing conversation is banter.

clue.text: West End in messy, chaotic organisation

indicators.note: chaotic letters are thrown into disorder
the end of the word West is its last letter

explanation.surface: London's West End is a messy, chaotic place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West End' looks like the London theatre district; End picks T from West. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A system is an orderly method or structure.

clue.text: A lens, say, to capture you, old girl

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means
ye is an old form of you
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Someone with a camera lens wants to photograph you, old girl.
